entries.title: The Christmas Truce Still Has Something to Teach Us About Leadership and Humanity
entries.standfirst: The 1914 truce was neither universal nor permanent. Its real power lies in what it shows about dignity, trust and human judgement inside rigid systems.
entries.seo_title: The Christmas Truce: Leadership, Trust and Humanity
entries.seo_description: Waithaka Ndegwa reflects on the verified history of the 1914 Christmas Truce and what it teaches about leadership, dignity and trust.

entries.title: From Reception Desk to Partnership: What Tong Wenhong’s Alibaba Story Really Teaches
entries.standfirst: The useful lesson is not a viral equity anecdote. It is how organisations notice capability, create internal mobility and share long-term value.
entries.seo_title: Tong Wenhong, Alibaba and the Value of Developing People
entries.seo_description: A current, verified look at Tong Wenhong’s Alibaba story and lessons on internal mobility, ownership, leadership and long-term value.

entries.title: Kenya Is Visa-Free — But Travel Is Not Paperwork-Free
entries.standfirst: Kenya’s open-travel ambition matters, but the current eTA exemptions, fees and 2026 traveller requirements show why policy should be judged by the real journey.
entries.seo_title: Kenya Visa-Free and eTA Rules in 2026: What Changed
entries.seo_description: Waithaka Ndegwa examines Kenya’s visa-free policy, current eTA exemptions and fees, and why travel friction matters for tourism, trade and integration.

entries.title: DHL’s Original Insight Still Matters: Remove Friction Before You Move More Goods
entries.standfirst: DHL began by moving documents ahead of cargo. For African enterprise, the enduring lesson is that infrastructure includes the processes that make movement reliable.
entries.seo_title: DHL’s Logistics Lesson for African Infrastructure and Enterprise
entries.seo_description: From DHL’s 1969 document-courier insight to its Africa investment, Waithaka Ndegwa explores logistics friction, infrastructure and enterprise opportunity.

entries.title: Sugar Beet Could Complement Kenya’s Sugarcane — But It Is Not Yet the Answer
entries.standfirst: Kenya’s sugar deficit, the end of the COMESA safeguard and the history of import quotas make diversification worth testing. Sugar beet may have a role—but only if agronomy, processing and economics are proven.
entries.seo_title: Sugar Beet in Kenya: Diversification Opportunity, Not Yet a Cure
entries.seo_description: Waithaka Ndegwa examines sugar beet in Kenya through the country’s sugar deficit, COMESA safeguard and quota history, and argues for evidence-led commercial pilots.

entries.title: Kenya’s Tomato Problem Is Not Just Overproduction — It Is a Processing and Coordination Gap
entries.standfirst: Less than 2% of locally produced tomatoes enter processing. The opportunity is to organise production around processing demand, not simply produce more and search for buyers later.
entries.seo_title: Kenya Tomato Farming: Processing, Cooperatives and Market Coordination
entries.seo_description: Waithaka Ndegwa revisits Kenya’s tomato gluts using current KALRO evidence and argues for processing, aggregation and market-led production.
